convoLines.text: "Can I tell you something? I know who took the extra rations but won't say."
"Come see what I found. You won't believe it."

"Thank you. ...I needed someone to know, and I needed it to stop there."
"I asked Ming about the pantry run — Ming's gone. Still need hands. Are you in?"
"I dreamed Ming was still here. Woke up angry at the dream. Stupid."
"About what they confided — yeah, we never did get back to that."
"Sleep's gone strange. I greet everyone by name each morning at odd hours now. Whatever gets me to morning."
"Okay. Yeah. I trust you."
"Go on, then. I'll be thinking good thoughts at you."
A comfortable quiet settles. They smile a little, and let it be.
"...Think about it? I'll be around."
They're smiling as you go. "Come back anytime."
"Listen. I need you to hear this before you go back out there. Just... be straight with me."
"You've seen what's out there. I'm just saying — the treeline at dusk. Don't."
"Promise me that. Please."
They nod slowly, not quite done, not quite continuing.
"Look, forget it. You wanted something?"
"This one is Patauá. Look at the leaf, feel the stem, breathe it in. It'll stick."
"Feral Paddy Rice. Remember the leaf, the stem, the smell — that's the whole of it."
"Ming is gone and the world just... continues. That's the part I can't stand."
"Someone should watch your back. Might as well be me."
You show them American Persimmon — where it grows, how to tell it apart. "Huh." They turn it over in their mind. "I'll remember that one."
"Alright — I should get back to it."
You say nothing. Neither do they, for a while — and it's fine.
"This was good." They mean it.
"Can I tell you something? I've been hiding an injury. I'm ashamed and I can't stop."
"Walk with me? I want another pair of eyes on something."
You walk to the tree line with Patrick. Nothing much there — but they talk the whole way, and you learn the shape of them a little better.
"I needed someone to know — just one person. Thank you for being that person, friend."
They go very still. Not relaxed-still. Held-still.
Patrick looks at you, level. "I told you the truth. You can keep poking it, but it's told."
The easy manner evaporates. What's left is watching you back.
"You're really going to make me say it again?" Patrick rubs their face. "Fine — but it's the same truth as last time."
They glance toward the fire, toward the others — checking who's listening.

Something crosses their face — quick, then gone. The practiced expression clicks back into place.

They nod — and keep their distance, for now.
"Most days I don't think about it. Today I am. Appreciate you noticing…"
"Mm." They don't look up from the fire, but they nod you down. "Sit."
"I should go. You know where to find me."

"Thanks for... you know. Just listening."
